title: Sigmoidoscopy
what: The doctor looks inside your rectum and the lower part of your large bowel with a tube that has a camera or light. A small tissue sample can be taken.
why: For blood in the stool, pain or itching around the anus, changes in bowel habits, before hemorrhoid treatment, or for screening.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; the report right away, tissue results in 5 to 10 days

prepare.title: Bowel prep
prepare.text: Usually an enema the evening before and in the morning, or a small enema. The clinic will give you the plan.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: The day before, a light dinner with no vegetables, fruit, or beans. In the morning, skip breakfast or have a light one. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide.

steps: You undress below the waist or put on disposable shorts
You lie on your left side with your knees to your chest
First, the doctor checks the anus with a finger
Then a lubricated tube is inserted, and a little air is added
The doctor looks at the bowel walls on a monitor
If needed, a small tissue sample is taken. This does not hurt
feel: Fullness and an urge to go to the toilet. This is from the air
If it hurts, tell the doctor
after: You will pass gas over the next hour
If a sample was taken, there may be a little blood in your stool for 1 to 2 days
red_flags: Severe belly pain, a hard belly, or a fever: call emergency services
Bleeding from the bottom with clots, or bleeding that will not stop: call emergency services

faq.q: How is this different from a colonoscopy?
faq.a: Sigmoidoscopy looks only at the lower part of the bowel, and the prep is simpler. A colonoscopy looks at the whole large bowel.

faq.q: Can I be asleep for it?
faq.a: It is usually done without sedation, since it is short. Ask the clinic.

reminders.text: Sigmoidoscopy tomorrow. This evening, do the enema or prep as your clinic told you.
